name: gpu
_doc: THE GPU BAND — 'which models write well on this box's GPU?'
A standing question, not a one-off experiment: add a leg whenever a model is
worth testing, run just that leg, and the summary still prints the whole band
(older legs are recalled from bench-results/ and labelled with their date).
LEG IDS ARE DURABLE — they are how a result is matched across runs. Renaming
one orphans its history; add a new id instead.

legs.label: BASELINE — Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT, as the app resolves it today
_why: The bar every other leg is measured against, and deliberately the ONLY leg
with no launch overrides: it loads exactly the way the app would load it
for you right now (computed fit + whatever tunes exist), so the baseline is
'the system as it works', not a hand-pinned config. What it resolved to is
recorded in the leg's load/measure output.
Every seeded preset points at this model, and its weights are already on disk.

legs.label: THINK ON — Gemma 4 26B-A4B QAT, reasoning enabled (A/B vs gpu-gemma-26b)
_why: The A/B partner to gpu-gemma-26b: SAME model, features and book — the only
difference is tunables.think = true. So the summary's A/B block isolates what
thinking COSTS (wall, tokens, draft acceptance) and, read against the baseline's
captures, what it CHANGES in the output. reasoning_budget = 1024 (seeded at the
base bundle + this box's hardware class) bounds it through the normal request
cascade — never a launch flag. llamaBench is null: the raw pp/tg matrix is
think-independent, so there is no point paying its ~5 min twice.

legs.label: HARD Q1, think OFF — the token↔Nine connection (multi-hop inference)
_why: The think A/B on a question that actually NEEDS reasoning (2026-07-21 robustness
fix): the original chat question was retrieval-summary — its answer sits in the
excerpts, so thinking had nothing to add. This one requires CONNECTING facts from
three ch1 scenes + ch2, none of which states the conclusion.
ANSWER KEY (judge against this, not vibes — full prose key in
docs/plans/2026-07-20-mtp-verify-think-ab-bench.md §7):
1. The shop lamp was tuned to / listening for a deeper-Facet note (the fork rang
near it, 'a note that leaned') — ch1 scene 1.
2. The commission-token hums 'exactly the note the lamp had leaned toward all
morning' — ch1 scene 2.
3. Corroboration: a street lamp gutters as the token passes on Kettle Lane (ch1
scene 3); the wrapped fork gives a muffled ring approaching the Nine (ch2 sc 1).
4. IMPLICATION (the reasoning step): the token resonates with a deep-Facet source
at/inside the Nine, so the 'routine structural clearance' is a deep-Facet site
— confirmed in ch2 scene 2 ('certify a deep-Facet wound as an empty warehouse').
A strong answer makes all three connections + the implication; a weak one retells
one scene. Runs 1..3: run 1 is cache-cold (timing only; quality unaffected).

legs.label: HARD Q2, think OFF — why the parties never came out (mechanism synthesis)
_why: Second hard question, different reasoning shape: MECHANISM synthesis across ch2+ch3
(the doc-2026-07-16 contradiction-finding style adapted to what the book contains).
ANSWER KEY (full prose in the plan doc §7):
1. The Nine loops one ~hour stretch — starts at seven past (Ode's stopped watch),
resets at the top of the hour — ch3 scene 2.
2. The reset pulls matter AND memory back: anyone who can't feel the deep Facets
'forgets the whole turn and lives it fresh' — ch3 scene 1.
3. So the three parties (Sedge's ledger, ch2 scene 1) never left: 'they're not
dead... still walking in. Every hour. For nine years' (ch3 sc 1); the third
party is in the east gallery believing it's the day they arrived (ch3 sc 2).
4. Ode remembers because deep-Facet sensitives stand 'slightly outside the loom'
and are NOT reset (ch3 sc 1) — the same exemption as Cael and Nettle.
A strong answer gives the loop mechanism + the forget rule + Ode's exemption; a
weak one says 'they were trapped' without the memory-reset mechanism.
